questions.text: निम्नलिखित लिगन्ड में से कौन-सा उभयदन्ती लिगन्ड है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following ligands is an ambidentate ligand?
questions.solution: SCN⁻ (thiocyanate ion) is an ambidentate ligand because it can coordinate to the central metal ion through either the sulphur atom (forming thiocyanato-S linkage) or the nitrogen atom (forming thiocyanato-N or isothiocyanato linkage). CO can only donate through carbon, NH₃ only through nitrogen, and H₂O only through oxygen; none of these have two different donor atoms, so they are not ambidentate.

questions.text: CoCl₃⋅4NH₃ के एक मोल में AgNO₃ विलयन मिलाने पर AgCl का एक मोल अवक्षेपित हुआ। Co की द्वितीयक संयोजकता है :
questions.text_english: On adding AgNO₃ solution to 1 mole of CoCl₃⋅4NH₃, one mole of AgCl is precipitated. The secondary valency of Co is:
questions.solution: When 1 mole of AgNO₃ precipitates 1 mole of AgCl, it means only 1 Cl⁻ is in the outer (ionisation) sphere. The formula is [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]Cl, so the complex contains 4 NH₃ and 2 Cl⁻ in the inner coordination sphere. According to Werner's theory, the secondary valency (coordination number) of Co equals the total number of ligands in the inner sphere: 4 NH₃ + 2 Cl⁻ = 6. Options B, C, and D give incorrect coordination numbers.

questions.text: संक्रमण तत्त्वों की 3d श्रेणी में निम्नलिखित में से किस तत्त्व की न्यूनतम ΔₐH° है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following elements of 3d series of transition elements has the lowest ΔₐH°?
questions.solution: Cu has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation (ΔₐH°) among the given 3d series elements. This is because Cu has a completely filled 3d subshell (3d¹° 4s¹), which results in weak metallic bonding and consequently lower energy is required to atomise it. Sc, Cr, and Zn have higher values; Zn also has a filled 3d shell but its overall metallic bonding is stronger than Cu.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया पर विचार कीजिए: (4-hydroxybenzyl alcohol + SOCl₂ → ?) प्राप्त मुख्य उत्पाद है :
questions.text_english: Consider the following reaction: 4-hydroxybenzyl alcohol treated with SOCl₂. The major product obtained is:

options.A: 4-chlorobenzyl chloride (CH₂Cl group and Cl at para position)
options.B: 4-hydroxybenzyl chloride (CH₂Cl group and OH at para position)
options.C: 4-chlorobenzyl alcohol (CH₂OH group and Cl at para position)
options.D: 2-chloro-4-hydroxybenzyl alcohol (CH₂OH group, Cl ortho, OH para)

options_english.A: 4-chlorobenzyl chloride (both OH and CH₂OH converted to Cl)
options_english.B: 4-hydroxybenzyl chloride (only CH₂OH converted to Cl, OH retained)
options_english.C: 4-chlorobenzyl alcohol (OH converted to Cl, CH₂OH retained)

questions.solution: SOCl₂ (thionyl chloride) converts alcoholic -OH groups to -Cl. The primary aliphatic alcohol group (-CH₂OH) reacts readily with SOCl₂ to give -CH₂Cl. Phenols are much less reactive towards SOCl₂ under normal conditions because the lone pair on oxygen is delocalized into the ring, making it less nucleophilic. Therefore, only the benzylic -CH₂OH is converted to -CH₂Cl, giving 4-hydroxybenzyl chloride as the major product (option B).

questions.text: cyclopentyl-CH₂–OH के विरचन के लिए मेथेनैल के साथ निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा ग्रीन्यार अभिकर्मक प्रयुक्त होगा ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following Grignard reagent will be used with methanal to prepare cyclopentyl-CH₂-OH?
questions.solution: To prepare cyclopentyl-CH₂-OH using methanal (HCHO), we need a Grignard reagent that, when added to HCHO, gives the product with one carbon added. The reaction is: RMgBr + HCHO → R-CH₂-OH (after hydrolysis). Since the target product is cyclopentyl-CH₂-OH, the R group is cyclopentyl. Therefore, the required Grignard reagent is cyclopentyl-MgBr (option A gives cyclopentyl-CH₂-OH). Wait — option A is cyclopentyl-CH₂MgBr which with HCHO gives cyclopentyl-CH₂-CH₂-OH. Option D (cyclopentyl-MgBr) with HCHO gives cyclopentyl-CH₂-OH. The correct answer is D.
questions.topic: Preparation of Alcohols using Grignard Reagent

questions.text: CH₃–O–CH₃ को जब HI के आधिक्य के साथ अभिकृत किया जाता है, तो वह देता है :
questions.text_english: CH₃–O–CH₃ when treated with excess HI gives:
questions.solution: Dimethyl ether (CH₃–O–CH₃) on treatment with excess HI first undergoes cleavage to give CH₃I and CH₃OH. Since HI is in excess, the methanol formed (CH₃OH) further reacts with HI to give another mole of CH₃I. Thus, the final products with excess HI are 2CH₃I. Options A gives only partial reaction (insufficient HI), B gives no substitution, and D would require different conditions.

questions.image_description: Option D shows aniline structure (benzene ring with NH₂ group).
questions.solution: Benzene sulphonyl chloride (C₆H₅SO₂Cl) reacts with primary amines (giving sulphonamide soluble in NaOH) and secondary amines (giving sulphonamide insoluble in NaOH). It does NOT react with tertiary amines like (C₂H₅)₃N because tertiary amines have no N–H bond available to undergo the reaction. Options B (primary amine), C (secondary amine), and D (primary amine) all have at least one N–H bond and will react.

questions.text_english: 'Scurvy' is caused by the deficiency of vitamin:
questions.solution: Scurvy is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid). Vitamin C is essential for the synthesis of collagen, a structural protein in connective tissues. Its deficiency leads to bleeding gums, loose teeth, and poor wound healing. Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness, Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets, and Vitamin E deficiency causes muscular dystrophy.

questions.text: किसी विलेय 'X' का 1% विलयन सूक्रोज (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 342 g mol⁻¹) के 6% विलयन के साथ समपरासारी है। विलेय 'X' का मोलर द्रव्यमान है :
questions.text_english: A 1% solution of solute 'X' is isotonic with a 6% solution of sucrose (molar mass = 342 g mol⁻¹). The molar mass of solute 'X' is:
questions.solution: For isotonic solutions, osmotic pressures are equal, meaning their molarities are equal. Molarity is proportional to (mass% / molar mass). So: (1 / Mₓ) = (6 / 342). Solving: Mₓ = (1 × 342) / 6 = 57 g mol⁻¹. The molar mass of solute X is 57 g mol⁻¹.

questions.text: 3 min⁻¹ वेग स्थिरांक (k) वाली किसी प्रथम कोटि की अभिक्रिया की अर्ध-आयु है :
questions.text_english: The half life of a first order reaction with rate constant (k) of 3 min⁻¹ is:
questions.solution: For a first order reaction, the half-life formula is t½ = 0.693 / k. Substituting k = 3 min⁻¹: t½ = 0.693 / 3 = 0.231 min. Options A (0.693) would be the answer if k = 1 min⁻¹, option B (2.31) if k = 0.3 min⁻¹, and option C (6.93) would incorrectly multiply rather than divide.

questions.text_english: Which of the following cells is used in hearing aids?
questions.solution: Mercury cells are used in hearing aids, watches, cameras, and other small devices that require a constant and reliable voltage over a long period. They provide a steady EMF of about 1.35 V throughout their life. Dry cells have varying voltage, nickel-cadmium cells are rechargeable and bulkier, and fuel cells require continuous fuel supply, making them unsuitable for hearing aids.

questions.text_english: Aniline on reaction with Bromine water gives:
questions.solution: Aniline reacts with bromine water to give 2,4,6-tribromoaniline as a white precipitate. The –NH₂ group is a powerful ortho/para director and strongly activates the benzene ring. With bromine water (aqueous bromine), all three activated positions (2, 4, and 6) are brominated simultaneously without requiring a Lewis acid catalyst. This reaction is used as a test for aniline. Options A, C, and D represent mono-substitution which requires controlled conditions using Br₂ in non-polar solvents.

questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): ΔₘᴵˢH and ΔₘᴵˢV are zero for an ideal solution.
Reason (R): The solution which obeys Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration is called an ideal solution.
questions.instruction_line: प्रश्न संख्या 13 से 16 के लिए, दो कथन दिए गए हैं — जिनमें एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है।

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।

options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

questions.solution: Both the Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. An ideal solution obeys Raoult's law over the entire concentration range, which means the interactions between solute-solvent molecules are identical to solute-solute and solvent-solvent interactions. As a result, there is no change in enthalpy on mixing (ΔₘᴵˢH = 0) and no change in volume on mixing (ΔₘᴵˢV = 0). The Reason directly explains why these quantities are zero for an ideal solution.

Assertion (A): Rate of reaction decreases with increase in temperature.
Reason (R): Number of effective collisions increases with increase in temperature.

options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation.

questions.solution: The Assertion (A) is false because in general, the rate of reaction increases with increase in temperature (not decreases). According to Arrhenius equation, higher temperature provides more energy to reactant molecules, increasing the fraction of molecules with energy equal to or greater than the activation energy. The Reason (R) is true — the number of effective collisions does increase with temperature. Since the Assertion is false but Reason is true, the answer is D.

sub_questions.text: (क) HI
sub_questions.text_english: (a) HI

key_points: Glucose reacts with HI to give n-hexane
All -OH groups are reduced and C=O is also reduced
Product: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (n-hexane)

sub_questions.solution: When glucose is treated with HI (hydroiodic acid), it undergoes reduction of all hydroxyl groups and the carbonyl group. The reaction proceeds as: C₆H₁₂O₆ + HI → n-hexane (CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃) + 6H₂O + 6HI (net). This confirms that glucose has a straight-chain structure with six carbon atoms, as the product is n-hexane.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) (CH₃CO)₂O

key_points: Glucose reacts with acetic anhydride to form glucose pentaacetate
All five -OH groups get acetylated
Product: Glucose pentaacetate (C₆H₇O(OCOCH₃)₅)

sub_questions.solution: Glucose reacts with acetic anhydride [(CH₃CO)₂O] to give glucose pentaacetate. All five free hydroxyl groups (-OH) present in the open-chain structure of glucose undergo acetylation. The reaction is: C₆H₇O(OH)₅ + 5(CH₃CO)₂O → C₆H₇O(OCOCH₃)₅ + 5CH₃COOH. This confirms the presence of five -OH groups in glucose.

OR
(b) What type of deviation is shown by ethanol and acetone mixture? Give reason. What type of azeotropic mixture is formed by that deviation?

sub_questions.text: (क) मोलल अवनमन स्थिरांक को परिभाषित कीजिए। यह गलन एन्थैल्पी से किस प्रकार संबंधित है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Define molal depression constant. How is it related to enthalpy of fusion?

key_points: Molal depression constant (Kf) is the depression in freezing point caused by 1 mole of solute in 1 kg of solvent
Kf = R × Tf² × M₁ / (1000 × ΔfusH)
Kf is inversely proportional to enthalpy of fusion

sub_questions.solution: The molal depression constant (Kf), also called cryoscopic constant, is defined as the depression in freezing point produced when 1 mole of a non-volatile, non-electrolyte solute is dissolved in 1 kilogram of the solvent. It is related to the enthalpy of fusion by the equation: Kf = R × Tf² × M₁ / (1000 × ΔfusH), where Tf is the freezing point of pure solvent, M₁ is the molar mass of solvent, and ΔfusH is the enthalpy of fusion. Higher the enthalpy of fusion, smaller is Kf.

sub_questions.text: (ख) एथेनॉल और ऐसीटोन मिश्रण द्वारा किस प्रकार का विचलन दर्शाया जाता है? कारण दीजिए। इस विचलन से किस प्रकार का स्थिरक्वाथी मिश्रण निर्मित होता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) What type of deviation is shown by ethanol and acetone mixture? Give reason. What type of azeotropic mixture is formed by that deviation?

key_points: Ethanol and acetone show positive deviation from Raoult's law
In pure ethanol, molecules are associated by H-bonds; acetone breaks these H-bonds
A–B interactions are weaker than A–A and B–B, vapour pressure increases
Minimum boiling azeotrope is formed

sub_questions.solution: Ethanol and acetone mixture shows positive deviation from Raoult's law. In pure ethanol, molecules are associated through strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds. When acetone is added, it breaks these hydrogen bonds (as acetone cannot form H-bonds with itself), making the interactions between ethanol and acetone (A–B) weaker than the original A–A interactions. This reduces the intermolecular forces, causing vapour pressure to be higher than expected. This positive deviation leads to the formation of a minimum boiling azeotrope.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) In a reaction, if the concentration of reactant 'X' is tripled, the rate of reaction becomes twenty-seven times. What is the order of the reaction?

key_points: Order of reaction = 3 (third order)

sub_questions.solution: If Rate = k[X]^n, then when [X] is tripled: new rate = k[3X]^n = 3^n × k[X]^n. Given that new rate = 27 × old rate, we have 3^n = 27 = 3³, so n = 3. The order of the reaction with respect to X is 3 (third order).

sub_questions.text: (ख) एक परिस्थिति बताइए जिसमें कोई द्विआण्विक अभिक्रिया गतिकत: प्रथम कोटि की अभिक्रिया होती है। ऐसी अभिक्रिया का एक उदाहरण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) State a condition under which a bimolecular reaction is kinetically a first-order reaction. Give an example of such a reaction.

key_points: When one reactant is present in large excess (pseudo-first order condition)
Example: Hydrolysis of ester (CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O → CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH)

sub_questions.solution: A bimolecular reaction behaves as a first-order reaction (pseudo-first order) when one of the reactants is present in large excess so that its concentration remains essentially constant throughout the reaction. Example: Hydrolysis of ethyl acetate — CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O → CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH. Here, water is in large excess, so its concentration remains constant, and the reaction follows first-order kinetics.

(क) निम्नलिखित युगल में से कौन-सा हैलोजन यौगिक Sₙ2 अभिक्रिया में तीव्रता से अभिक्रिया करेगा और क्यों ?
(ख) आर्थो- और पैरा- स्थितियों पर नाइट्रो समूह की उपस्थिति हैलोऐरीनों की नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया के प्रति अभिक्रियाशीलता क्यों बढ़ा देती है ?
questions.text_english:
(a) Which halogen compound in the following pair will react faster in Sₙ2 reaction and why?
(b) Why does the presence of nitro groups at ortho- and para- positions in haloarenes increase their reactivity towards nucleophilic substitution reaction?

sub_questions.text: (क) निम्नलिखित युगल में से कौन-सा हैलोजन यौगिक Sₙ2 अभिक्रिया में तीव्रता से अभिक्रिया करेगा और क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Which halogen compound in the following pair will react faster in Sₙ2 reaction and why? (neopentyl chloride vs isobutyl chloride)

key_points: Isobutyl chloride (less hindered primary halide) reacts faster
SN2 is favoured by less steric hindrance at the carbon bearing the leaving group

sub_questions.solution: In SN2 reactions, steric hindrance at the carbon bearing the leaving group is the deciding factor. The compound with less branching near the site of attack reacts faster. Isobutyl chloride (2-methylpropyl chloride, (CH₃)₂CHCH₂Cl) will react faster than neopentyl chloride ((CH₃)₃CCH₂Cl) because neopentyl chloride has a bulky tert-butyl group adjacent to the reacting carbon, severely hindering backside attack by the nucleophile. Isobutyl chloride is less hindered, allowing easier nucleophilic approach.

sub_questions.text: (ख) आर्थो- और पैरा- स्थितियों पर नाइट्रो समूह की उपस्थिति हैलोऐरीनों की नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया के प्रति अभिक्रियाशीलता क्यों बढ़ा देती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Why does the presence of nitro groups at ortho- and para- positions in haloarenes increase their reactivity towards nucleophilic substitution reaction?

key_points: Nitro groups at ortho/para positions withdraw electron density from the ring by resonance
This increases the partial positive charge on the carbon bearing the halogen
Nucleophilic attack becomes easier

sub_questions.solution: Nitro groups are strong electron-withdrawing groups that withdraw electron density from the benzene ring by resonance. When placed at ortho or para positions relative to the halogen, they directly withdraw electron density from the carbon bearing the halogen through resonance, increasing the partial positive charge (electrophilicity) on that carbon. This makes it easier for a nucleophile to attack. Meta-nitro groups cannot withdraw electrons from that carbon through resonance and hence have a much smaller effect.

questions.solution: See sub-questions (a) and (b) for detailed answers.
questions.topic: SN2 Reactions and Nucleophilic Substitution in Haloarenes

questions.text:
(क) 2-ब्रोमोब्यूटेन के जल-अपघटन से (±)-ब्यूटेन-2-ऑल बनने में किस प्रकार की नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन (Sₙ1 अथवा Sₙ2) होती है? कारण दीजिए।
(ख) क्या होता है जब क्लोरोबेन्ज़ीन और मेथिल क्लोराइड को शुष्क ईथर में सोडियम धातु के साथ अभिकृत किया जाता है ?
questions.text_english:
(a) What type of nucleophilic substitution (Sₙ1 or Sₙ2) occurs in the hydrolysis of 2-Bromobutane to form (±)-Butan-2-ol? Give reason.
(b) What happens when chlorobenzene and methyl chloride are treated with sodium metal in dry ether?

sub_questions.text: (क) 2-ब्रोमोब्यूटेन के जल-अपघटन से (±)-ब्यूटेन-2-ऑल बनने में किस प्रकार की नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन (Sₙ1 अथवा Sₙ2) होती है? कारण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) What type of nucleophilic substitution (Sₙ1 or Sₙ2) occurs in the hydrolysis of 2-Bromobutane to form (±)-Butan-2-ol? Give reason.

key_points: SN1 mechanism occurs
2-bromobutane has a secondary carbon; forms secondary carbocation intermediate
Racemic mixture (±) is formed because nucleophile attacks planar carbocation from both sides equally

sub_questions.solution: SN1 mechanism occurs in the hydrolysis of 2-bromobutane to give (±)-butan-2-ol. The reason is that 2-bromobutane is a secondary alkyl halide, and secondary carbocations can form as intermediates in the SN1 pathway. The carbocation at C-2 is planar (sp² hybridised), so the nucleophile (water) can attack from either face with equal probability, leading to the formation of both R and S configurations in equal amounts — a racemic mixture (±). If SN2 occurred, only inversion would give a single enantiomer.

sub_questions.text: (ख) क्या होता है जब क्लोरोबेन्ज़ीन और मेथिल क्लोराइड को शुष्क ईथर में सोडियम धातु के साथ अभिकृत किया जाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) What happens when chlorobenzene and methyl chloride are treated with sodium metal in dry ether?

key_points: Wurtz-Fittig reaction occurs
C₆H₅Cl + CH₃Cl + 2Na → C₆H₅CH₃ + 2NaCl
Product: Toluene (methylbenzene)

sub_questions.solution: This is the Wurtz-Fittig reaction. When chlorobenzene and methyl chloride are treated with sodium metal in dry ether, toluene (methylbenzene) is formed. The reaction is: C₆H₅Cl + CH₃Cl + 2Na → C₆H₅CH₃ + 2NaCl. Sodium removes the halogen from both compounds and couples the aryl and alkyl groups together.

questions.solution: See sub-questions (a) and (b) for detailed answers.

(a) Write the reactions involved in the following:
(i) Reimer-Tiemann reaction
(ii) Kolbe's reaction
(b) Name the reagent used in the bromination of phenol to form 2,4,6-Tribromophenol.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Write equations for Reimer-Tiemann reaction and Kolbe's reaction.

key_points: Reimer-Tiemann: C₆H₅OH + CHCl₃ + NaOH → 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde)
Kolbe's: C₆H₅ONa + CO₂ (pressure, 400K) → sodium salicylate → + H⁺ → salicylic acid

sub_questions.solution: Reimer-Tiemann Reaction: When phenol is treated with chloroform (CHCl₃) in the presence of NaOH followed by acidification, an aldehyde group (-CHO) is introduced at the ortho position: C₆H₅OH + CHCl₃ + 3NaOH → 2-HOC₆H₄CHO (salicylaldehyde) + 3NaCl + 2H₂O. Kolbe's Reaction: Sodium phenoxide when heated with CO₂ under pressure at 400 K, followed by acidification, gives salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid): C₆H₅ONa + CO₂ → (pressure, 400 K) → HOC₆H₄COONa → (H⁺) → HOC₆H₄COOH.

key_points: Bromine water (Br₂/H₂O)

sub_questions.solution: Bromine water (aqueous bromine, Br₂/H₂O) is the reagent used. When phenol is treated with bromine water, the highly activated ring undergoes electrophilic substitution at all three ortho and para positions, directly giving 2,4,6-tribromophenol as a white precipitate, without requiring a Lewis acid catalyst.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) CH₃CH₂Cl →(KCN) A →(LiAlH₄) B →(HNO₂, 0°C) C

key_points: A = CH₃CH₂CN (propanenitrile)
B = CH₃CH₂CH₂NH₂ (propan-1-amine)
C = CH₃CH₂CH₂OH (propan-1-ol) [primary amine reacts with HNO₂ to give alcohol]

sub_questions.solution: CH₃CH₂Cl reacts with KCN (nucleophilic substitution) to give A = CH₃CH₂CN (propanenitrile). A is reduced by LiAlH₄ to give B = CH₃CH₂CH₂NH₂ (propan-1-amine, a primary amine). B (primary amine) reacts with HNO₂ at 0°C to form an unstable diazonium salt which immediately decomposes to give C = CH₃CH₂CH₂OH (propan-1-ol) + N₂ + HCl.

sub_questions.text: (ख) Nitrobenzene →(Fe/HCl) A →(NaNO₂ + HCl, 273 K) B →(C₆H₅OH) C
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Nitrobenzene →(Fe/HCl) A →(NaNO₂ + HCl, 273 K) B →(C₆H₅OH) C

key_points: A = Aniline (C₆H₅NH₂)
B = Benzenediazonium chloride (C₆H₅N₂⁻Cl⁻)
C = Diphenyl ether / Phenyl azo phenol (azo coupling product)

sub_questions.solution: Nitrobenzene is reduced by Fe/HCl to give A = Aniline (C₆H₅NH₂). Aniline is diazotised with NaNO₂ + HCl at 273 K (0°C) to give B = Benzenediazonium chloride (C₆H₅N₂⁻Cl⁻). Benzenediazonium chloride undergoes azo coupling with phenol (C₆H₅OH) at the para position to give C = p-hydroxyazobenzene (an orange-yellow azo dye), C₆H₅–N=N–C₆H₄OH.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Benzoic acid to Benzaldehyde

key_points: Benzoic acid → (SOCl₂) → Benzoyl chloride → (H₂/Pd-BaSO₄, Rosenmund reduction) → Benzaldehyde

sub_questions.solution: Benzoic acid is first converted to benzoyl chloride by treatment with thionyl chloride (SOCl₂): C₆H₅COOH + SOCl₂ → C₆H₅COCl + SO₂ + HCl. Benzoyl chloride is then subjected to Rosenmund reduction (H₂ gas over Pd/BaSO₄ catalyst in the presence of quinoline): C₆H₅COCl + H₂ → C₆H₅CHO + HCl. The BaSO₄ and quinoline act as catalyst poisons to prevent over-reduction to toluene.

sub_questions.text: (ख) ऐथेनैल से प्रोपेनोन
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Ethanal to Propanone

key_points: Ethanal → (HCN) → CH₃CH(OH)CN → (H₃O⁺) → CH₃CH(OH)COOH → oxidation is not direct
Alternatively: Ethanal → (CH₃MgBr then H₃O⁺) → propan-2-ol → (oxidation) → propanone

sub_questions.solution: Ethanal (CH₃CHO) is converted to propanone (CH₃COCH₃) via the following steps: First, CH₃CHO is treated with methylmagnesium bromide (CH₃MgBr, a Grignard reagent), then hydrolysed to give propan-2-ol: CH₃CHO + CH₃MgBr → CH₃CH(OMgBr)CH₃ → (H₂O) → CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ (propan-2-ol). Propan-2-ol is then oxidised using pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇: CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ → CH₃COCH₃ (propanone).

sub_questions.text: (ग) ऐसीटोफ़ीनोन से बेन्ज़ोइक अम्ल
sub_questions.text_english: (c) Acetophenone to Benzoic acid

key_points: Acetophenone → (Cl₂/NaOH, iodoform/haloform reaction) → benzoic acid + CHCl₃

sub_questions.solution: Acetophenone (C₆H₅COCH₃) undergoes the haloform reaction when treated with Cl₂ and NaOH (or I₂ and NaOH). The methyl ketone is oxidised and the CH₃ group is replaced by CHX₃. The reaction gives sodium benzoate which on acidification gives benzoic acid: C₆H₅COCH₃ + 3Cl₂ + 4NaOH → C₆H₅COONa + CHCl₃ + 3NaCl + 3H₂O. Then C₆H₅COONa + HCl → C₆H₅COOH + NaCl.

PhMgBr is then treated with ethanal (CH₃CHO) followed by aqueous hydrolysis: C₆H₅MgBr + CH₃CHO → C₆H₅CH(OMgBr)CH₃ → (H₂O) → C₆H₅CH(OH)CH₃ (1-phenylethanol).

questions.text: 200 g जल में किसी अवाष्पशील विलेय के 5 g को घोलकर विलयन बनाया गया। 300 K पर इसका वाष्प दाब 31.84 mm Hg है। विलेय का मोलर द्रव्यमान परिकलित कीजिए। (300 K पर शुद्ध जल का वाष्प दाब = 32 mm Hg)
questions.text_english: A solution is prepared by dissolving 5 g of a non-volatile solute in 200 g of water. It has a vapour pressure of 31.84 mm Hg at 300 K. Calculate the molar mass of the solute. (Vapour pressure of pure water at 300 K = 32 mm Hg)

key_points: Relative lowering of vapour pressure = (P° – Ps)/P° = x₂ (mole fraction of solute)
Molar mass of solute = 41.1 g mol⁻¹ (approx)

questions.solution: Using Raoult's law: (P° – Ps)/P° = x₂ (mole fraction of solute). (32 – 31.84)/32 = 0.16/32 = 0.005. Moles of water (solvent) n₁ = 200/18 = 11.11 mol. Let molar mass of solute = M. Moles of solute n₂ = 5/M. So 0.005 = (5/M) / (11.11 + 5/M). Since 5/M is very small: 0.005 ≈ (5/M)/11.11, giving M = 5/(0.005 × 11.11) = 5/0.05556 ≈ 90 g mol⁻¹. (Exact calculation: 0.005(11.11 + 5/M) = 5/M → 0.05556 + 0.005(5/M) = 5/M → 0.05556 = 5/M – 0.025/M = 4.975/M → M = 4.975/0.05556 ≈ 89.5 g mol⁻¹.)
questions.topic: Vapour Pressure and Molar Mass Calculation

questions.text: 0.2 M KCl विलयन की चालकता 2.48 × 10⁻² S cm⁻¹ है। इसकी मोलर चालकता और वियोजन मात्रा (α) परिकलित कीजिए। दिया गया है: λ°ᵏ⁺ = 73.5 S cm² mol⁻¹, λ°ᴸₗ⁻ = 76.5 S cm² mol⁻¹
questions.text_english: The conductivity of 0.2 M solution of KCl is 2.48 × 10⁻² S cm⁻¹. Calculate its molar conductivity and degree of dissociation (α). Given: λ°ᵏ⁺ = 73.5 S cm² mol⁻¹, λ°ᴸₗ⁻ = 76.5 S cm² mol⁻¹

key_points: Λ°ₘ = λ°ᵏ⁺ + λ°ᴸₗ⁻ = 73.5 + 76.5 = 150 S cm² mol⁻¹

questions.solution: Molar conductivity Λₘ = (κ × 1000) / M = (2.48 × 10⁻² × 1000) / 0.2 = 24.8/0.2 = 124 S cm² mol⁻¹. Molar conductivity at infinite dilution: Λ°ₘ (KCl) = λ°ᵏ⁺ + λ°ᴸₗ⁻ = 73.5 + 76.5 = 150 S cm² mol⁻¹. Degree of dissociation α = Λₘ/Λ°ₘ = 124/150 = 0.827 (i.e., 82.7%). This means approximately 82.7% of KCl is dissociated at this concentration.
questions.topic: Molar Conductivity and Degree of Dissociation

questions.text:
संक्रमण तत्त्वों के स्वभाव के संदर्भ में (n–1)d इलेक्ट्रॉनों की भागीदारी इन तत्त्वों को कुछ विशिष्ट गुण प्रदान करती है। अत: परिवर्ती ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाओं के अतिरिक्त संक्रमण धातुएँ अनुचुम्बकीय गुण और उत्प्रेरक गुण दर्शाती हैं तथा रंगीन आयन बनाने की प्रवृत्ति पाई जाती है। संक्रमण धातुएँ बहुत सी अधातुओं, जैसे ऑक्सीजन, नाइट्रोजन तथा हैलोजनों से अभिक्रिया करती हैं। KMnO₄ और K₂Cr₂O₇ इनके सामान्य उदाहरण हैं।

आंतरिक संक्रमण तत्त्वों की दो श्रेणियाँ लैन्थेनॉयड तथा एक्टिनॉयड आवर्त सारणी के f-ब्लॉक की रचना करती हैं। लैन्थेनॉयडों में 4f-कक्षक के इलेक्ट्रॉनों के अपूर्ण परिरक्षण प्रभाव (imperfect shielding effect) के कारण परमाणु क्रमांक में वृद्धि के साथ परमाणु आमाप में क्रमिक ह्रास होता है जिसके कारण आकुंचन होता है।
questions.text_english:
The involvement of (n–1)d electrons in the behaviour of transition elements impart certain distinct characteristics to these elements. Thus, in addition to variable oxidation states, they exhibit paramagnetic behaviour, catalytic properties and tendency for the formation of coloured ions. The transition metals react with a number of non-metals like oxygen, nitrogen and halogens. KMnO₄ and K₂Cr₂O₇ are common examples.

The two series of inner transition elements, lanthanoids and actinoids, constitute the f-block of the periodic table. In the lanthanoids, there is regular decrease in atomic size with increase in atomic number due to the imperfect shielding effect of 4f-orbital electrons which causes contraction.

sub_questions.text: (क) संक्रमण धातुएँ तथा उनके यौगिक अच्छे उत्प्रेरक की भाँति क्यों कार्य करते हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Why do transition metals and their compounds act as good catalysts?

key_points: Transition metals have variable oxidation states and ability to form intermediate compounds
They provide a suitable surface for adsorption of reactants

sub_questions.solution: Transition metals act as good catalysts because they have variable oxidation states that allow them to form intermediate compounds with reactants and then release the products, regenerating themselves. They also possess suitable metallic surfaces that can adsorb reactant molecules, bringing them close together and lowering the activation energy. These two properties together make them highly effective catalysts.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) What is the cause of contraction in the atomic size of lanthanoids?

key_points: Imperfect shielding effect of 4f electrons
4f electrons shield nuclear charge poorly, so effective nuclear charge increases with atomic number, causing contraction

sub_questions.solution: The contraction in atomic size of lanthanoids (lanthanoid contraction) is caused by the poor or imperfect shielding effect of 4f electrons. The 4f orbitals have a complex shape and do not shield the nuclear charge effectively from the outer electrons. As atomic number increases, protons are added to the nucleus but the 4f electrons added do not shield adequately, so the effective nuclear charge experienced by the outer electrons increases steadily, pulling them closer and causing a regular decrease in atomic size.

(c) Define lanthanoid contraction. How does it affect the atomic radii of the third transition series and the second transition series?
OR
(c) In aqueous media, which is a stronger reducing agent — Cr²⁺ or Fe²⁺ and why?

key_points: Lanthanoid contraction: regular decrease in ionic/atomic radii of lanthanoids with increasing atomic number
Due to lanthanoid contraction, 3rd transition series elements have nearly same radii as 2nd transition series (e.g., Zr and Hf have almost equal radii)
OR: Cr²⁺ is a stronger reducing agent than Fe²⁺ because Cr³⁺ has a stable half-filled 3d³ configuration

sub_questions.solution: Lanthanoid contraction is defined as the steady decrease in the size (atomic and ionic radii) of lanthanoid elements with increasing atomic number, due to the imperfect shielding of 4f electrons causing a progressive increase in effective nuclear charge. Effect on transition series: Because of lanthanoid contraction, the elements of the third transition series (5d) have almost the same atomic radii as the corresponding elements of the second transition series (4d). For example, Zr and Hf have nearly identical radii (~155 pm), making their chemical separation very difficult. OR: Cr²⁺ is a stronger reducing agent than Fe²⁺ in aqueous medium. Cr²⁺ is readily oxidised to Cr³⁺, which has a stable half-filled d³ configuration (t₂g³), making the Cr²⁺ → Cr³⁺ oxidation thermodynamically favourable. Fe²⁺ oxidises to Fe³⁺ (d⁵, half-filled), which is also stable but the driving force is less than for Cr.

Proteins are the most abundant biomolecules of the living system. Proteins are the polymers of about twenty different α-amino acids which are linked by peptide bonds. sub_questions.solution: The zwitter ionic form (also called dipolar ion) of amino acids is the internal salt formed when the basic amino group (-NH₂) accepts a proton to become -NH₃⁺, and simultaneously the acidic carboxyl group (-COOH) donates a proton to become -COO⁻, within the same molecule. NaOH) → C₆H₅CH=CHCOCH₃ (4-phenylbut-3-en-2-one). sub_questions.text_english: (ii) Chemical tests to distinguish: (1) Acetophenone and Propiophenone; (2) Pentanal and Pentan-3-one

key_points: (1) Iodoform test: Acetophenone (CH₃CO–) gives yellow iodoform precipitate; Propiophenone (C₂H₅CO–) does not
(2) Tollens/Fehling test: Pentanal (aldehyde) gives silver mirror or red precipitate; Pentan-3-one (ketone) does not

sub_questions.solution: (1) Acetophenone vs Propiophenone: Perform iodoform test — treat each with I₂ and NaOH. Acetophenone (C₆H₅COCH₃) contains the CH₃CO– group and gives a yellow precipitate of iodoform (CHI₃). Propiophenone (C₆H₅COC₂H₅) does not have the CH₃CO– group and gives no iodoform test. (2) Pentanal vs Pentan-3-one: Perform Tollens' test — treat each with ammoniacal AgNO₃. Pentanal (an aldehyde) reduces Ag⁺ to Ag, giving a silver mirror on the walls of the tube. Pentan-3-one is a ketone and does not reduce Tollens' reagent; no silver mirror is formed.

sub_questions.text_english: (b)(i) Give reasons: (1) Only one NH₂ in semicarbazide reacts; (2) Acetaldehyde more reactive than acetone towards HCN

key_points: (1) Other NH₂ is deactivated by resonance with the adjacent C=O of semicarbazide
(2) Acetaldehyde has less steric hindrance and less electron density on carbonyl carbon than acetone

sub_questions.solution: (1) Semicarbazide (H₂N–CO–NH–NH₂) has two amino groups. The –NH₂ attached directly to the –CO– group is deactivated because its lone pair is delocalised into the C=O by resonance (–NH₂ → –NH=C–O⁻), making it less nucleophilic. Only the terminal –NH₂ (attached to the other N) retains its nucleophilicity and reacts with the carbonyl compound to form semicarbazone. (2) Acetaldehyde (CH₃CHO) is more reactive than acetone (CH₃COCH₃) towards nucleophilic addition of HCN because: (a) Acetaldehyde has only one methyl group, so the carbonyl carbon is less sterically hindered than in acetone (which has two methyl groups). (b) Two methyl groups in acetone donate more electron density to the carbonyl carbon by inductive effect, making it less electrophilic and hence less susceptible to nucleophilic attack.

sub_questions.solution: (ii)(1) Decreasing order of acidic strength: O₂N–CH₂–COOH > HCOOH > CH₃COOH. The nitro group (–NO₂) is strongly electron-withdrawing, stabilising the carboxylate anion of O₂NCH₂COOH, making it the strongest acid. HCOOH has no alkyl group to donate electrons, while CH₃COOH has an electron-donating methyl group that destabilises the carboxylate, making it the weakest. sub_questions.solution: In the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction, a carboxylic acid with an α-hydrogen is treated with chlorine or bromine in the presence of a small amount of red phosphorus (P). The α-hydrogen is replaced by a halogen atom. For example: CH₃COOH + Cl₂ → (P, red) → ClCH₂COOH + HCl. sub_questions.solution: In a tetrahedral complex of the type [MA₂B₂], all four positions around the central metal atom are equivalent. Any two ligands of one type are always adjacent (there is no position that can be 'opposite' another in a tetrahedron as in a square planar complex). sub_questions.text_english: (d) Write the hybridization and magnetic character of the complex [Ni(CO)₄] on the basis of valence bond theory. [Atomic No.: Ni = 28]

key_points: Ni has configuration [Ar]3d¸ 4s²; in Ni(0), configuration is 3d¹°

Diamagnetic (all electrons paired in 3d¹°)

sub_questions.solution: Nickel has atomic number 28. Configuration of Ni: [Ar] 3d¸ 4s². In [Ni(CO)₄], Ni is in the zero oxidation state (Ni°), so its configuration is 3d¹° (electrons from 4s pair into 3d). CO is a strong field ligand that causes complete pairing of 3d electrons. The 4 CO ligands donate electron pairs into 4 equivalent sp³ hybrid orbitals. Hybridisation: sp³, tetrahedral geometry. Since all 3d electrons are paired (3d¹°), [Ni(CO)₄] is diamagnetic.

key_points: (i) [Co(C₂O₄)₃]³⁻ is more stable (oxalate is a chelating bidentate ligand, chelate effect)
(ii) [CoF₆]³⁻ is the high spin complex (F⁻ is a weak field ligand)

sub_questions.solution: (i) [Co(C₂O₄)₃]³⁻ is more stable. Oxalate (C₂O₄²⁻) is a bidentate chelating ligand, and the chelate effect significantly increases the stability of complexes formed by chelating ligands due to the entropic advantage of chelation. (ii) [CoF₆]³⁻ is the high spin complex because F⁻ is a weak field ligand that produces a small Δ₀, which is less than the pairing energy (P). Electrons occupy the higher energy eᴳ orbitals before pairing in t₂ᴳ, leading to a high spin configuration.

sub_questions.text: (च) उभयदन्ती लिगन्ड और द्विदन्तुर लिगन्ड में क्या अंतर है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (f) What is the difference between an ambidentate ligand and bidentate ligand?

key_points: Ambidentate: single donor atom but can coordinate through either of two different atoms (e.g., SCN⁻ through S or N)
Bidentate: two donor atoms that both coordinate simultaneously to the metal (e.g., en, oxalate)

sub_questions.solution: An ambidentate ligand is a unidentate ligand that has two different donor atoms but coordinates through only one of them at a time. For example, SCN⁻ can bind through S (thiocyanato-S) or N (thiocyanato-N/isothiocyanato). A bidentate ligand, on the other hand, has two donor atoms that both simultaneously coordinate to the central metal ion, forming a chelate ring. For example, ethylenediamine (H₂N–CH₂–CH₂–NH₂) binds through both nitrogen atoms at once.

sub_questions.text: (छ) अष्टफलकीय क्षेत्र में d⁵ का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास t₂ᴳ और eᴳ के पदों में लिखिए जब: (i) Δ0 > P, और (ii) Δ0 < P
sub_questions.text_english: (g) Write the electronic configuration of d⁵ in terms of t₂g and eg in an octahedral field when: (i) Δ₀ > P, and (ii) Δ₀ < P

key_points: (i) Δ₀ > P (strong field): t₂g⁵ eg⁰ (low spin, all 5 electrons in t₂g)
(ii) Δ₀ < P (weak field): t₂g³ eg² (high spin, one electron in each orbital)

sub_questions.solution: For a d⁵ configuration in an octahedral field: (i) When Δ₀ > P (pairing energy), the crystal field splitting energy is greater than the energy required to pair electrons, so electrons prefer to pair in the lower energy t₂g orbitals rather than occupy the higher eg orbitals. Configuration: t₂g⁵ eg⁰ (low spin complex, 1 unpaired electron). (ii) When Δ₀ < P, the pairing energy is greater than the splitting, so electrons occupy all five d-orbitals singly before pairing (Hund's rule). Configuration: t₂g³ eg² (high spin complex, 5 unpaired electrons).

(a)(i) Calculate emf of the following cell at 25°C: Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(0.001M) || Cd²⁺(0.1 M) | Cd(s). Given: E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V, E°(Cd²⁺/Cd) = −0.40 V [log 10 = 1]

sub_questions.text: (ii) फ़ैराडे का द्वितीय नियम बताइए। NaCl विलयन के विद्युत-अपघटन पर pH।
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) State Faraday's second law of electrolysis. How will pH of aqueous NaCl be affected on electrolysis?

key_points: Faraday's second law: masses of different substances deposited by same quantity of electricity are in ratio of their equivalent masses
Electrolysis of NaCl(aq): Cl⁻ discharged at anode (Cl₂ gas), H₂O oxidised; at cathode H⁺ reduced to H₂, leaving OH⁻
pH increases (solution becomes alkaline) due to accumulation of NaOH

sub_questions.solution: Faraday's Second Law of Electrolysis: When the same quantity of electricity is passed through different electrolytes, the masses of substances deposited at respective electrodes are directly proportional to their chemical equivalent masses (equivalent weight). Effect on pH during electrolysis of aqueous NaCl: At the cathode: 2H₂O + 2e⁻ → H₂ + 2OH⁻ (or 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂). At the anode: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. The net result is generation of OH⁻ ions near the cathode and removal of Cl⁻; the solution around the cathode becomes alkaline (NaOH forms). Therefore, the pH of the solution increases (becomes more alkaline) upon electrolysis.

sub_questions.text: (ख)(i) ΔrG° और log Kc परिकलित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b)(i) Calculate ΔrG° and log Kc for: Fe(s) + Ag⁺(aq) ⇌ Fe²⁺(aq) + Ag(s).
sub_questions.solution: E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = E°(Ag⁺/Ag) – E°(Fe²⁺/Fe) = 0.80 – (−0.44) = +1.24 V. Here n = 1 (1 electron transferred). ΔrG° = –nFE° = –(1)(96500)(1.24) = –119,660 J mol⁻¹ ≈ –119.66 kJ mol⁻¹. log Kc = nE°/0.0591 = (1 × 1.24)/0.0591 = 1.24/0.0591 ≈ 20.98. So Kc = 10²¹ (approximately).

sub_questions.text: (ii) ईंधन सेलों के प्राथमिक और द्वितीयक बैटरियों की अपेक्षा कोई दो लाभ।
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) Write any two advantages of fuel cells over primary and secondary batteries.

key_points: High efficiency (60-70%) as they directly convert chemical energy to electrical energy
Pollution-free: by-product is only water when H₂/O₂ fuel cells are used

sub_questions.solution: Two advantages of fuel cells over primary and secondary batteries are: (1) Higher efficiency — fuel cells can convert chemical energy directly into electrical energy with efficiency of 60–70%, which is much higher than conventional batteries or heat engines. (2) Eco-friendly operation — hydrogen-oxygen fuel cells produce only water as a by-product, making them non-polluting. They also operate continuously as long as fuel is supplied, unlike batteries that need recharging or replacement.

sub_questions.text: (iii) 1 मोल H₂O के O₂ में ऑक्सीकरण के लिए कितने फ़ैराडे आवश्यक होंगे ?
sub_questions.text_english: (iii) How many Faradays are required for the oxidation of 1 mole of H₂O to O₂?

key_points: 2 Faradays are required per mole of H₂O

sub_questions.solution: The oxidation of H₂O to O₂ occurs at the anode: 2H₂O → O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻. This means 4 moles of electrons (4 Faradays) are required to oxidise 2 moles of H₂O to 1 mole of O₂. Therefore, for 1 mole of H₂O: Faradays required = 4/2 = 2 Faradays.
